what: Tier 2 may not be reference-bound after all, and our own selection rule would hide it
registered_at: 2026-10-30 06:22 UTC, untested -- recorded as an idea with its evidence
the_claim_i_made_and_now_doubt: I wrote that Tier 2 is reference-bound because our entry (0.46522) sits just under our cleaner's own score against truth (0.4755), so the policy is already tracking as well as its reference allows.
what_contradicts_it: Tier 3 shows a policy CAN beat its reference, and not marginally: eleven of thirty clips have negative headroom, meaning the achieved trajectory is closer to truth than the reconstruction the policy was driven by. e19's policy beat its reconstruction by 183 cm. The mechanism is physics -- contact, gravity and the support surface constrain the object to plausible poses, while a noisy or wrong reference is unconstrained. Tier 2's noise (1.94 cm, 21.4 deg) is exactly the physically implausible kind: objects tilted or floating in ways contact would forbid. The leader's 0.56768 sits ABOVE our cleaner's 0.4755 ceiling, which is what beating your own reference looks like.
the_implied_arm: LOOSEN object tracking on Tier 2 rather than tighten it, so physics dominates: widen object_position std or cut its weight, and let contact place the object while the policy follows the hand and body. This is the opposite of our shipping recipe, which tightened std from 0.2 to 0.08 to track the reference HARDER -- a choice made to chase MP-SR, before we knew policies can exceed their references.
the_sharp_problem_it_exposes: Our registered Tier 2 selection rule is input-only: it adopts the rollout CLOSER to the noisy input. A physics-corrected rollout is deliberately FARTHER from that input while being closer to truth. So the rule would reject exactly the rollouts this arm is built to produce. That is not a hypothetical: on Tier 3, e17's input-only verdict adopted a rollout whose truth AUC fell (results/t3_e17_negative_headroom.json). The rule is sound where the input is better than the policy and blind where it is worse.
what_would_have_to_change: Selection. The tier constrains what the POLICY may read at inference, not how we choose among our own rollouts, and Kaggle hands out leaderboard feedback five times a day regardless. Measured on Tier 3, reading truth to choose was worth only +0.00135 of AUC and LOST on MPPE -- but that was with arms that track their reference. With a physics-correcting arm the gap could be the whole 0.10 to first place.
cost_to_test: A warm start from a shipped Tier 2 actor with a loosened object term is ~$0.50 per clip, so three clips is ~$1.50 -- the cheapest untested idea left on any tier. It is not being run now because the remaining credit is committed to T1XFER, and splitting it would leave neither arm with a usable sample.
how_to_judge_it: Score against truth and report both selections. If a loosened arm beats its own reference on even one clip, Tier 2 is not reference-bound and the input-only rule needs revisiting before the next entry -- and that revision, not the arm, would be the finding.
